mainTopic: The sister's כרת, separate חטאות for separate לאוין, and how the משנה counts its 36 כרת sins
overview: This amud finishes a discussion about why the Torah wrote a separate כרת for one's sister. The רבנן say it teaches that we do not punish based on a קל וחומר. רבי יצחק uses it to teach separate חטאות when one woman is his sister, his father's sister and his mother's sister. רבי הושעיא teaches that two separate לאוין sharing one כרת still require separate חטאות, as with blending and smearing the anointing oil. רב נחמן בר יצחק proves this from the order of the משנה. The גמרא then asks how the משנה reaches 36 כרת sins. רבי יוחנן says the list counts a man's sins, following רבי ישמעאל. רב says 33 are a man's חטאות and 3 more are added to complete the list of כרת sins. Next, the גמרא explains why שבת and עבודה זרה each count as one item. It then searches for a real case of mistaken idol worship, and that search continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The רבנן: the sister's כרת teaches about a full sister
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, the extra כרת for a sister is needed for a sister from both father and mother. It teaches that we do not punish based on a logical inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: The extra כרת is for his sister who is both his father's daughter and his mother's daughter. It teaches that we do not give a punishment just based on a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer about the רבנן: what do they learn from the separate כרת written about a sister? They say it teaches the law of a full sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah clearly forbids a half-sister from the father's side and a half-sister from the mother's side. You might think a full sister is forbidden "all the more so," but a punishment cannot come from that kind of reasoning. The Torah has to write it out, and that is what this verse does.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving a punishment based on a logical inference (a קל וחומר) instead of an explicit verse
A sister from both the same father and the same mother (a full sister)
Spiritual 'cutting off,' the Torah's punishment for certain intentional sins

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the full sister is permitted without this verse! She is certainly forbidden. The question is only whether the Torah's punishment can be applied to her through reasoning alone. The רבנן say it cannot, so the Torah wrote it explicitly.

phrases.notes: "מן הדין" here means a קל וחומר, an "all the more so" argument.

steps.title: רבי יצחק holds we do punish from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק does not need the verse for the full sister. He holds that a punishment can be learned from a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק holds that we do punish based on an inference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יצחק is free to use the sister's כרת for a different lesson (dividing the חטאות).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a punishment can come from a קל וחומר, the full sister's כרת is already known by reasoning. So the extra verse is free to teach something else. This is the first of two possible explanations for his view.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / is of the opinion

phrases.english: And רבי יצחק holds:

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק holds that a punishment can be learned from a קל וחומר

steps.title: Another option: רבי יצחק learns the punishment from the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation of רבי יצחק: he learns the full sister's punishment from the warning (the לאו) that the Torah already wrote about her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say this: he learns the punishment from the warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different reason why רבי יצחק does not need the extra verse for a full sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if we do not punish from a קל וחומר, the prohibition (אזהרה) for the sister already includes a full sister. רבי יצחק connects the punishment to that prohibition. So again, the extra כרת is free for his own lesson.

steps.title: רבי הושעיא: two prohibitions with one כרת need separate חטאות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes רבי הושעיא. Whenever there are two separate prohibitions but only one כרת is written for both, each one requires its own חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי הושעיא: Anywhere you find two prohibitions and only one כרת, divide the חטאת between them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It gives a general rule for counting חטאות when someone does several sins by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think one כרת means one sin, and so only one חטאת. רבי הושעיא says the number of separate לאוין decides it. Two separate prohibitions mean two חטאות, even if they share one כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Negative commandments ("do not" prohibitions)
Divide the sin offering, meaning a separate חטאת for each sin
A sin offering, brought for doing by mistake a sin that carries כרת

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule leads straight to the next challenge. If separate לאוין already cause separate חטאות, then the sister's כרת seems unneeded for that purpose.

steps.title: The example: blending and applying the anointing oil
steps.stepSummary: The case is one who blends the anointing oil and one who smears it on a person. There are two separate prohibitions but only one כרת verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is this? Blending the anointing oil and applying it. It is written: "Upon the flesh of man it shall not be applied, and according to its composition..." That is two prohibitions. There is one כרת, as it is written: "Whoever compounds any like it, or whoever puts any of it upon a stranger, he shall be cut off from his people."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where this rule applies, and answers with the case of the anointing oil (שמן המשחה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse gives two separate prohibitions: do not apply the oil to a person, and do not make oil with its recipe. The next verse covers both acts with a single כרת. So by רבי הושעיא's rule, doing both by mistake requires two חטאות.

steps.title: Then why is the sister's כרת needed?
steps.stepSummary: If separate prohibitions already require separate חטאות, then the עריות, which each have their own לאו, already get separate חטאות. So why did the Torah write a separate כרת for the sister?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the prohibitions are separate, why do I need the כרת that the Torah wrote for one's sister?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי הושעיא's rule to challenge רבי יצחק's reading, which said the sister's כרת teaches separate חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the עריות has its own separate לאו, and they share one general כרת. By רבי הושעיא's rule, that alone already gives a separate חטאת for each. So רבי יצחק's lesson from the sister's כרת seems unnecessary, and the verse looks extra again. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate, distinct prohibitions
"The Merciful One," meaning the Torah / ה׳
"Why do I need it?" It asks why a verse or detail is needed

phrases.english: But since the prohibitions are separate,

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The עריות each have a separate לאו and share one כרת, so רבי הושעיא's rule already gives separate חטאות. That makes the sister's כרת unnecessary for this lesson.

steps.title: The extra sister verse teaches a different lesson for each opinion
steps.stepSummary: The separate כרת for the sister is needed. For the רבנן it teaches אין עונשין מן הדין. For רבי יצחק it teaches separate liability when one woman is his sister, his father's sister and his mother's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יצחק the verse teaches one thing, based on his own view. According to the רבנן, they need the verse to teach that we do not punish based on a קל וחומר. According to רבי יצחק, he uses it to make a man liable for intercourse with his sister who is also his father's sister and also his mother's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6, which asked why the תורה wrote a separate כרת for the sister. It explains that each opinion uses that verse for its own lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that without this verse we might punish the sister using a קל וחומר, so the verse teaches אין עונשין מן הדין. רבי יצחק does not need the verse for that, as steps 2 and 3 showed. So he uses it for a new point: one woman who falls under several forbidden relationships brings several separate חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not give a punishment based only on a logical קל וחומר
According to his own view
His father's sister (his aunt on his father's side)
His mother's sister (his aunt on his mother's side)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן and רבי יצחק argue about what the verse literally says. They agree the verse is needed. They only disagree about which lesson it comes to teach.

steps.title: Where the רבנן learn the rule of separate liability
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn the rule of separate חטאות for the triple sister from the first word אחותו in the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, where do they learn this law? They learn it from the word 'his sister' at the beginning of the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the רבנן learn רבי יצחק's lesson about separate חטאות, and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא 20:17 says 'אחותו' twice. The רבנן use the first one, at the start of the verse, to teach that the three relationships are counted separately. That leaves the כרת part of the verse free to teach אין עונשין מן הדין.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part (of the verse)
They derive it

phrases.english: And the רבנן?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source the רבנן use for separate חטאות for the triple sister

steps.title: Why רבי יצחק uses the second word 'his sister'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק holds that the first אחותו is just the normal way the verse tells the story. So he learns the separate liability from the second אחותו at the end of the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק? He holds that 'his sister' at the start is just the normal style of the verse. So he learns separation from 'his sister' at the end of the verse: to separate the liability for his sister who is also his father's sister and also his mother's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יצחק does not learn from the first אחותו, as the רבנן do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יצחק, the first אחותו is needed just to describe the case, so no extra lesson can come from it. The second אחותו, near the כרת part, is the extra one. It teaches לחלק, which means counting each relationship as a separate sin.

keyTerms.meaning: The normal style of the verse, not an extra word for a new lesson
To separate, so each sin brings its own חטאת
The last part (of the verse)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a triple sister brings separate חטאות. They only argue which word of the verse teaches it. The רבנן use the first אחותו, and רבי יצחק uses the second one.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes the משנה as support
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says our משנה supports רבי אלעזר. It lists blending the oil, blending the incense, and smearing the oil, in that order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We also learned this in the משנה: One who blends the oil, one who blends the incense, and one who smears with the anointing oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי אלעזר's rule from steps 4 and 5. רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes the list in the משנה, which sets up the proof he explains in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said that blending the anointing oil and smearing it bring two separate חטאות. רב נחמן בר יצחק points to the משנה's list of כרת sins as support. The proof itself comes from the order of the list, which the next step explains.

The incense of the בית המקדש

steps.title: Why incense is placed in the middle of the list
steps.stepSummary: The משנה put blending the incense between the two oil cases to teach that both oil cases are separate sins, just like the incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the משנה to put 'one who blends the incense' in the middle? Isn't it teaching us this: just as the incense has its own לאו and one gets כרת for it by itself, so too blending the oil and smearing it, since each has its own לאו, one is liable for each by itself?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains his proof: the strange order of the משנה shows that the two oil cases count as two separate sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה should have listed the two oil cases next to each other. It placed the incense between them on purpose, to compare them to the incense. The incense is clearly its own sin with its own כרת, so the two oil cases, each with its own לאו, are also separate sins with separate חטאות. This supports רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: In the middle
Isn't this what it comes to teach us?
By itself, as a separate sin

steps.whatToRemember: The order of a משנה can teach a law. Putting the incense between the two oil cases shows that blending the oil and smearing it are two separate sins, each needing its own חטאת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This backs up רבי אלעזר's rule from step 4: when two separate לאוין share one written כרת, each one still requires its own חטאת.

steps.title: Maybe the order just keeps the blending cases together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible push-back: maybe the משנה put the incense case in the middle only so that the two blending cases sit next to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that the תנא simply wanted to list the two blending cases together...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone attacking רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof. It offers a simpler reason for the order of the משנה. This line sets up the next step, which knocks the push-back down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, blending the incense comes right after blending the oil. Someone could say the order has nothing to do with separate חטאות. Maybe the תנא just grouped the two kinds of blending, and that is why the incense landed between the two oil cases.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another reason the order could have been chosen: to keep the two blending cases next to each other.

steps.title: A reversed order would have kept both pairs together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא could have written incense first, then blending the oil, then smearing the oil. That order keeps the blending cases together and the oil cases together. Choosing to split the oil cases must teach that they are separate חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him list them in reverse: one who blends the incense, one who blends the oil, and one who smears the anointing oil. Why did he split up the oil cases? Is it not to teach us that there are separate חטאות between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the push-back. A different order would have grouped the blending cases without breaking up the oil cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With incense first, both blending cases stay next to each other, and both oil cases stay next to each other. The תנא did not choose that order. He split the two oil cases on purpose, so the order must be telling us something: the two oil cases are separate sins, each needing its own חטאת, just like the incense.

Separate liability: a separate חטאת for each sin
One who smears or applies the oil

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof for רבי אלעזר airtight.

phrases.english: Let him teach them in reverse order:
one who blends the incense,
and one who blends the oil,
and one who smears the anointing oil.
Why did he split up the oil?
Is it not that this teaches us
that there are separate sin offerings between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push-back of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the order only exists to keep the blending cases together.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A reversed order would have done that just as well without splitting the oil cases, so the split must be intentional.

steps.title: Conclusion: the proof for רבי אלעזר stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it that this is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that the משנה supports רבי אלעזר. This closes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blending the oil and smearing the oil are separate sins. Someone who does both in one forgetting brings two חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the גמרא accepts the proof

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה splits the two oil cases (blending and smearing) with the incense case. This teaches they are separate חטאות, as רבי אלעזר said.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof as defended in step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Blending the anointing oil and smearing it carry separate חטאות, as רבי אלעזר said.

steps.title: Whose sins is the משנה counting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's case of a man with a male and asks what the basis of the משנה's count is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who lies with a male. On what basis is the תנא counting?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's case of a man who lies with a male and asks whose sins the list is counting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יוחנן said the count of 36 teaches something: one person who did all of them in one forgetting brings a חטאת for each one. So the 36 must be sins that one single person could do. The גמרא asks: is that person a man or a woman?

keyTerms.meaning: A man who lies with a male
On what basis is he counting?

phrases.english: One who lies with a male.
The תנא, on what basis is he counting?
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's total of 36 כריתות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the proof about the oil is finished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the list of 36 counts sins done by a man or by a woman.

steps.title: Neither men nor women give 36
steps.stepSummary: If the list counts men's sins, the woman with an animal drops out and the list is one short. If it counts women's sins, the two male cases drop out and it is two short.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he counts men's sins, take out the woman who lies with an animal, and the count is one short! If he counts women's sins, take out the man who lies with a male and with an animal, and the count is two short!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that both choices fail. Either way, the list does not reach 36.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man cannot do the sin of a woman with an animal, so a list of men's sins has only 35. A woman cannot do the sins of a man with a male or a man with an animal, so a list of women's sins has only 34.

keyTerms.meaning: Men
Women
Remove, take out
Is lacking, falls short
A woman who lies with an animal

phrases.english: If he counts men,
take out the woman who lies with an animal,
and the count is short by one!
If he counts women,
take out of them the one who lies with a male
and with an animal,
and the count is short by two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out why the question in step 15 is hard to answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No single person, man or woman, can do all 36 sins on the list, so the count does not work either way.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: men are counted, and lying with a male is two sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the list counts men's sins. The woman's case is replaced with a man who lets a male lie with him. This follows רבי ישמעאל, who says that is a second, separate חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Really, the תנא counts men, and he teaches it this way: one who lies with a male, and one who brings a male upon himself. This follows רבי ישמעאל, who says he is liable for two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the problem. He keeps the count for men and swaps in a different case in place of the woman with an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the woman's case, the men's list has 35. רבי יוחנן fills the empty spot by splitting the male case into two: the active man and the passive man. That works only according to רבי ישמעאל, who holds a man who does both in one forgetting brings two חטאות. That brings the count back to 36.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeps one side of the question and defends it)
And teach it this way (read the משנה differently)
And he brought a male upon himself (the passive partner)
Liable for two (two חטאות)

steps.whatToRemember: The 36 count is for men's sins. In place of the woman with an animal, the list has a man who lies with a male and a man who lets a male lie with him. These are two separate sins, according to רבי ישמעאל.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not adding a 37th case. He takes the woman's case out and puts the passive male case in its place, so the total stays 36.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Really, the תנא is counting men,
and teach it like this:
one who lies with a male
and brought a male upon himself,
phrases.notes: This replaces the case of the woman with an animal, so the total stays 36.

phrases.english: and this follows רבי ישמעאל,
who says: he is liable for two.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם תַּנָּא גַּבְרֵי קָחָשֵׁיב וְתָנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה differently, following one תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list cannot belong to men, because then it has only 35.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list is men's. The woman's case is replaced by the passive male case, which counts separately according to רבי ישמעאל, so the total is 36.

steps.title: The end of the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, so the beginning should too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. The מגדף case at the end of the משנה was explained like רבי עקיבא, which suggests the beginning is also רבי עקיבא, not רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches the blasphemer in its later part, and we explain that part like רבי עקיבא. So the first part should also be רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's answer. It points out that the משנה has already been tied to רבי עקיבא because of the מגדף case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We normally assume one משנה follows one תנא from start to finish. The מגדף case at the end was explained like רבי עקיבא, so the opening cases should be רבי עקיבא as well. But רבי יוחנן built his count on רבי ישמעאל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: One who blasphemes, cursing ה׳'s name
The later part of a משנה
The first part of a משנה
We set it up, meaning we explain the case according to a certain view

phrases.english: But since it teaches the blasphemer in its later part,
and we explain it according to Rabbi Akiva,
the first part is also Rabbi Akiva!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer from step 17, which relied on רבי ישמעאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא (מגדף) follows רבי עקיבא, so the רישא should follow רבי עקיבא too, not רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: A suggestion: maybe רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי ישמעאל on this point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the whole משנה is רבי עקיבא, and on this one point רבי עקיבא holds like רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the משנה is רבי עקיבא, and in the first part he holds like רבי ישמעאל...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out: the whole משנה is רבי עקיבא, and he simply agrees with רבי ישמעאל here. This suggestion is only a setup, because the גמרא knocks it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי עקיבא agreed that a man who lets a male lie with him brings a separate חטאת, there would be no conflict at all. The whole משנה could follow רבי עקיבא and still count that case.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. It introduces a suggested answer, often one that will be rejected
He holds like..., meaning he agrees with another sage's view on a specific point

phrases.english: And if you will say: it is Rabbi Akiva,
and in the first part he holds like Rabbi Yishmael,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggests that both views agree on this point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to have to follow either רבי עקיבא or רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: It could follow רבי עקיבא throughout, if he agrees with רבי ישמעאל on this case.

steps.title: רבי אבהו shows רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that רבי ישמעאל learns the two acts from two פסוקים, so there are two חטאות. רבי עקיבא learns both from one פסוק, so there is only one חטאת. The suggestion fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אבהו said: if a man lies with a male and also lets a male lie with him, then according to רבי ישמעאל, who learns these from two פסוקים ("Do not lie with a male" and "There shall not be a קדש among Israel"), he brings two חטאות. According to רבי עקיבא he brings only one, because he learns both from one פסוק: "Do not lie with a male" can also be read as "Do not be lain with."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 19. It quotes רבי אבהו, who says clearly that רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל argue about this exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separate חטאות come from separate prohibitions. רבי ישמעאל finds the passive act in its own פסוק (קדש), so it is a second sin. רבי עקיבא reads both the active and the passive act into one פסוק, so it is one sin. That means רבי עקיבא could never count it as an extra item in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Two separate פסוקים
Here, a man who lets another male lie with him
Liable for two, meaning two separate חטאות
Read into it, meaning read the same letters with different vowels

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the number of חטאות depends on how many separate prohibitions there are. One act can count once or twice depending on how the פסוקים are read.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Abbahu say:
One who lies with a male
and brought a male upon himself,
phrases.notes: He means the same man was also the passive one, letting another male lie with him.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דְּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ מִתַּרְתֵּי קְרָאֵי,
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yishmael, who derives it from two verses,
from "And you shall not lie with a male,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:22

phrases.english: and from "And there shall not be a קדש among the sons of Israel" –
phrases.notes: דברים 23:18

phrases.english: he is liable for two,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת,
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Akiva he is liable for only one,
since he derives it from one verse:
"You shall not lie with a male,"
read it as: "You shall not be lain with!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion from step 19 that רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the משנה is entirely רבי עקיבא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא learns both acts from one פסוק, so for him they are only one חטאת and could not be an extra item.

steps.title: Splitting the משנה between two תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the first part of the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, and only on the מגדף case does the משנה follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the first part is רבי ישמעאל, and about the blasphemer he holds like רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, and on the one issue of מגדף it agrees with רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of making רבי עקיבא agree with רבי ישמעאל, the גמרא flips it around. The author of the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל's count and accepts רבי עקיבא's view only on מגדף. This keeps רבי יוחנן's answer standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier idea and brings a new one
The first part follows רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: Rather: the first part is Rabbi Yishmael,
and regarding the blasphemer he holds like Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 20 rejected the first suggestion, this offers a new answer to the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the משנה to one תנא who agrees with another sage on one point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the מגדף case, the whole משנה seemed to be רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is רבי ישמעאל, who agrees with רבי עקיבא only about מגדף.

steps.title: If so, why not list the two animal cases too?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, it should also list a man who lies with an animal and a man who lets an animal lie with him as two separate items.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it also teach: one who lies with an animal, and one who brings an animal upon himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer from step 21. If the list follows רבי ישמעאל's way of counting, it seems to be missing cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a male, רבי ישמעאל counts the active and passive acts as two separate sins. The same split should work with an animal. So the משנה should list both animal cases, but it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. It takes the last answer and shows a problem it creates
Let it also teach. The question is why the משנה left something out
An animal

phrases.english: If so, let it also teach:
one who lies with an animal,
and one who brings an animal upon himself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 21 that the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the first part of the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל's two-prohibition approach should also give two separate items for an animal, yet the משנה does not list them.

steps.title: אביי: Even רבי ישמעאל Counts Only One Offering for the Animal Cases
steps.stepSummary: אביי teaches that a man who lies with an animal and also lets an animal lie with him brings only one חטאת, even according to רבי ישמעאל. The extra פסוק רבי ישמעאל uses speaks only about men.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't אביי say: a man who lies with an animal and lets an animal lie with him is liable for only one offering, even according to רבי ישמעאל, because the extra פסוק was written about men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last question. The משנה does not need to list the two animal cases separately, because even רבי ישמעאל counts them as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל gets a second חטאת for the passive act from an extra פסוק. אביי points out that this פסוק speaks only about a man with a man, not a man with an animal. So for the animal cases there is only one prohibition and one חטאת, even for רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who lies with an animal (the active act)
He lets an animal lie with him (the passive act)
He is liable for only one offering
It is written about men, meaning a man with another man

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי disagrees with רבי ישמעאל about men. רבי ישמעאל still gives two חטאות for a man with a man. אביי is only saying the extra פסוק does not reach the animal case.

phrases.english: But didn't Abaye say:
one who lies with an animal
and brings an animal upon himself,
even according to Rabbi Yishmael
is liable for only one [offering],
because when the verse is written, it is written about men.
phrases.notes: He means the extra פסוק that רבי ישמעאל uses for the passive act. It talks about a man with a man, not about an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22 by showing the premise is wrong: רבי ישמעאל does not split the animal case into two.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the premise: the extra פסוק does not apply to the animal case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי ישמעאל counts two חטאות for a man with a man, he should count two for the animal case too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra פסוק is written only about men, so the animal case brings one חטאת even for רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: רב: The משנה Lists 33 Offering Cases Plus 3 Extra כרת Cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, in the name of רב, gives a new way to read the משנה. The תנא lists 33 sins that bring a חטאת and adds 3 more that carry כרת to finish the list of כרת sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רב: The תנא teaches thirty-three חטאות, and he teaches three more כריתות to complete the list of כרת sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different approach to the count of the משנה. Not every item on the list has to bring a חטאת; three are there only because they carry כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא tried to make every item fit one person's set of חטאות. רב says this is not needed. 33 items are sins for which a man brings a חטאת, and 3 items that don't fit that group were added so the full list of כרת sins is complete. This removes the pressure to make every case fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה
Sin offerings brought for an accidental sin
Sins punished with כרת, being cut off
To complete them, to finish the list

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how we read the whole list of 36. Not every item has to bring a חטאת, so a case that doesn't fit the חטאת rule can still be on the list.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rav:
The tanna teaches thirty-three sin offerings,
and he teaches three [cases of] karet,
to complete them with karet cases.
phrases.notes: These three don't fit the 33 cases where a man brings a חטאת. They were added so the list of כרת sins is complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבי יוחנן approach is settled, a second approach to the משנה's count is offered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה lists 33 sins for which a man brings a חטאת, and adds 3 more כרת cases that fall outside that group, to complete the list of כרת sins.

steps.title: Proof: פסח and מילה Are Positive מצוות on the List
steps.stepSummary: Support for רב: the end of the משנה lists פסח and מילה, which are positive מצוות. Why would they be listed at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: For the end of the משנה teaches: פסח and מילה, which are positive מצוות. Why does it teach פסח and מילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב's approach. It points to two items at the end of the list that look different from all the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other item is a sin you do. פסח and מילה are things you fail to do, and they carry כרת. Their presence suggests the list is not only about חטאת cases, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the משנה
The קרבן פסח
Circumcision
A positive מצוה, something you must do

phrases.english: For the latter part teaches:
the Pesach offering and circumcision, which are positive מצוות.
Why does it teach the Pesach offering and circumcision?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings evidence from the משנה itself for רב's approach in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that some items in the list carry כרת without bringing a חטאת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the משנה lists פסח and מילה, which are positive מצוות

steps.title: A Positive מצוה Cannot Bring a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: Maybe פסח and מילה are listed to teach that you bring a קרבן for them? No. A ברייתא teaches that the whole Torah is compared to עבודה זרה, which shows when a קרבן is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say they are listed to teach that you bring a קרבן for them, does one bring one? But a ברייתא teaches: the whole Torah is compared to עבודה זרה, as it is written: "You shall have one law for one who acts by mistake. But the soul that acts with a high hand."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away a possible way out of the proof. Someone might say פסח and מילה are listed because they bring a קרבן, and the גמרא starts to show that this is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If פסח and מילה brought a קרבן, they would fit the חטאת list and the proof for רב would fail. The ברייתא compares the whole Torah to עבודה זרה, so a קרבן is brought only for a sin that is like עבודה זרה. The full reasoning continues right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought to the בית המקדש
Was compared to, linked in the פסוק
Idol worship
By mistake, without knowing
With a high hand, on purpose and defiantly

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not finish the argument. The ברייתא keeps going after the פסוק, and only then do we see why a positive מצוה cannot bring a קרבן.

phrases.english: And if you say: to bring an offering for them,
does one bring [one]?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: הוּקְּשָׁה כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: The entire Torah is compared to idol worship,
as it is written: "You shall have one law
for one who acts by mistake.
But the soul that acts with a high hand" –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Protects the proof of Step 25 by rejecting another reason פסח and מילה might be listed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that פסח and מילה are listed because they bring a קרבן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קרבן is brought only for sins compared to עבודה זרה, as the ברייתא learns from the פסוק, and a positive מצוה does not fit that.

steps.title: Only 'Don't-Do' Sins Bring a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: just as עבודה זרה is a 'sit and don't do' prohibition, every sin that brings a חטאת must be a 'sit and don't do' prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as עבודה זרה is a case of 'sit and don't do,' so too every sin that brings a חטאת must be a case of 'sit and don't do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step. It shows that a חטאת comes only for breaking a prohibition, never for skipping a positive מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה is the model for every חטאת. It is a 'don't do' sin, so only 'don't do' sins bring a חטאת. Skipping פסח or מילה means failing to do something, so no קרבן can come for them. That rejects the idea that the משנה lists them to teach that they bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship, the model case for every חטאת
'Sit and don't do': a prohibition, where you keep the rule by not acting
So too (compares one case to another)

phrases.aramaic: מָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: Just as idol worship is a case of 'sit and do not act,'
so too, every case must be 'sit and do not act'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that step 26 began quoting.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that פסח and מילה are listed in the משנה to teach that they bring a קרבן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חטאת comes only for a 'don't do' prohibition, like עבודה זרה. פסח and מילה are positive מצוות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule for every חטאת in the Torah: it is brought only for doing a forbidden act by mistake.

steps.title: The Proof for רב Stands
steps.stepSummary: So the משנה must list 33 sins that bring a חטאת and then add 3 more כרת sins just to complete the list of כרת sins. The proof works.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't it proven that the תנא listed 33 sins that bring a חטאת for someone who does them by mistake, and then listed 3 more כרת sins to complete the list of כרת sins? Yes, it is proven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof for רב. Since פסח and מילה can't bring a קרבן, they must be in the משנה only to complete the list of כרת sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was only one other reason the משנה might list פסח and מילה: to teach that they bring a קרבן. Step 27 ruled that out. So רב's reading must be right: 33 items bring a חטאת, and 3 are added only because they carry כרת. The גמרא accepts the proof with 'שמע מינה'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Learn from it': the proof works
By mistake, without meaning to sin
Being 'cut off', a punishment from Heaven
To complete them, to finish the list

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has 36 items. 33 are sins for which a man brings a חטאת for a mistake. 3 more כרת cases that fall outside that group are added to complete the list: a woman with an animal, פסח, and מילה.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it correct to learn from this:
he taught thirty-three sin offerings
for someone who does them by mistake,
and then he taught three more כרת cases
to complete the list of כרת sins,
phrases.notes: The three are a woman with an animal, פסח, and מילה.

phrases.english: Learn from it: yes, that's right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 27's rule to finish the proof begun in step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב is right: the משנה lists 33 sins for which a man brings a חטאת, plus 3 more כרת cases outside that group, added to complete the list of כרת sins.

steps.title: How Can שבת Be Just One Item?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists 'one who breaks שבת' as one item. But there are 39 kinds of forbidden work on שבת, and each one brings its own חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה lists 'one who breaks שבת.' The חכמים ask: but שבת has thirty-nine kinds of forbidden work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's item 'one who breaks שבת' and challenges it. שבת has 39 kinds of work, so how can it count as a single item?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the 39 kinds of work can bring its own חטאת. If so, שבת alone would be more items than the whole list of 36. So why does the משנה count it as one?

keyTerms.meaning: One who breaks שבת
Forty minus one, meaning the 39 kinds of forbidden work on שבת

phrases.english: The משנה says: 'One who breaks שבת.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: שַׁבָּת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת הָוְויָין!
phrases.english: They say: but שבת has forty minus one kinds of work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a single item on the משנה's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה counting 'one who breaks שבת' as a single item.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are 39 kinds of work, each with its own חטאת, so שבת should count as many items, not one.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: He Forgot It Was שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה means someone who forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden. A person like that brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the תנא is talking about someone who forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden. He is liable for only one חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question from step 29. The משנה is talking about one special case of breaking שבת, and in that case there is only one חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His mistake was only about which day it was. He knew every kind of work was forbidden on שבת. Since he made one mistake, he brings one חטאת no matter how many kinds of work he did. That is why שבת counts as one item.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake about שבת: he didn't know or forgot it was שבת
On purpose about the work: he knew these kinds of work were forbidden
One

steps.confusionAlert: שבת still has 39 kinds of work. In other cases each one can bring its own חטאת. Here there is only one חטאת because there was only one mistake: he forgot what day it was.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The תנא taught a mistake about שבת, but on purpose about the kinds of work,
phrases.notes: He forgot it was שבת, but he knew these kinds of work are forbidden on שבת.

phrases.english: where he is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: תַּנָּא שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה means one specific way of breaking שבת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the משנה meant breaking שבת in general, which could mean up to 39 separate חטאות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means someone who forgot it was שבת. He brings only one חטאת, so שבת counts as one item.

steps.title: A ברייתא Backs Up רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק's word 'הנה' (many sins) together with 'אחת' (one). It applies this to someone who forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'הנה' (many) that are 'אחת' (one) means someone who forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a source for רבי יוחנן. It reads the פסוק to show that many kinds of work can count as just one sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the חטאת says 'מאחת מהנה,' 'one of them.' The ברייתא learns that sometimes 'הנה,' many acts, count as 'אחת,' one sin. That happens when he forgot it was שבת, because all his acts come from one mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Them': many acts
'One': one sin and one חטאת
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who forgot it was שבת brings only one חטאת, even if he did many kinds of work. That is why the משנה counts שבת as one item.

phrases.english: As a ברייתא teaches:
'Them' (many acts) that is 'one' —
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק 'מאחת מהנה' (ויקרא 4:2).

phrases.english: this is a mistake about שבת, but on purpose about the kinds of work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for רבי יוחנן's answer in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that someone who forgot it was שבת brings only one חטאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads the words 'מאחת מהנה' in ויקרא 4:2.

steps.title: Why not teach the case that brings 39 offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה did not teach the case of knowing it was שבת but not knowing the work was forbidden, where the person brings 39 חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the משנה teach the case where he knew it was שבת but did not know the kinds of work were forbidden. That person is liable for 39 offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer. If the משנה is choosing one case of שבת, why not pick the case with 39 חטאות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the משנה means someone who forgot it was שבת, who brings only one חטאת. The גמרא points to the opposite case: he knew it was שבת but did not know each work was forbidden. That person brings a separate חטאת for each of the 39 kinds of work, so it seems a more fitting case to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing something knowingly
Doing something by mistake, without knowing
The kinds of forbidden work on שבת
Forty minus one, which is 39

phrases.english: But let it teach: knowing about שבת
but not knowing about the kinds of work
where he is liable for forty minus one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's choice of case from step 30
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation that the משנה means someone who forgot it was שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה is choosing a case, the case with 39 חטאות seems more worth teaching than the case with only one.

steps.title: ברייתות that support the 39-offering case
steps.stepSummary: Two ברייתות show that sometimes one brings a separate offering for each sin, and that this applies when one knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And he does one of them.' Sometimes he is liable one offering for all of them, and sometimes he is liable for each one. And another ברייתא teaches: 'one' that is 'many.' This is when he knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its question with ברייתות. They show that the 39-offering case is a real, known case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא learns from the פסוק that a person can bring either one offering for everything or one offering for each act. The second ברייתא names the case of many offerings: he knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden. This makes the question from step 32 stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
Each and every one
'One' that counts as 'many': one prohibition that brings many offerings

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And he does one of them"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:2

phrases.english: sometimes he is liable one offering for all of them

phrases.aramaic: וּפְעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: and sometimes he is liable for each and every one.
And it is taught: "one" that is "many"
knowing about שבת but not knowing about the kinds of work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the 39-offering case used in the question
steps.raayaObject: That someone who knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden brings a separate חטאת for each kind of work
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות reading the פסוק 'וְעָשָׂה מֵאַחַת מֵהֵנָּה'

steps.title: The תנא preferred the one-offering case
steps.stepSummary: The תנא chose the case of forgetting שבת to teach that even someone who did the work knowingly still brings at least one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא preferred the case where he forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden, because it teaches that he is at least not exempt from a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 32. The תנא picked the forgetting-שבת case on purpose, because it teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person knew the work was forbidden, so we might think he is not a mistaken sinner at all and brings nothing. The משנה teaches that he still brings at least one חטאת. That lesson is the reason the תנא chose this case over the 39-offering case.

keyTerms.meaning: He prefers it, it is better in his eyes
At least
Exempt, free from an obligation

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה counts שבת as one item because it means someone who forgot it was שבת. The תנא chose that case to teach that he still brings one חטאת, even though he knew the work was forbidden.

phrases.english: The תנא: forgetting it was שבת
but knowing about the kinds of work, this case he prefers
because at least he is not exempt from a חטאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת עֲדִיפָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 32 and 33
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the תנא chose this case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 39-offering case seems more worth teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forgetting-שבת case teaches a bigger lesson: even one who knew the work was forbidden still brings a חטאת.

steps.title: The משנה teaches עבודה זרה the same way
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses the same kind of case for עבודה זרה: he did not know it was idol worship but knew those acts of worship were forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise you find regarding עבודה זרה. The משנה teaches the case where he did not know it was idol worship but knew about the acts of worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the תנא picks the same kind of case for עבודה זרה. This supports the answer in step 34.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עבודה זרה the משנה also teaches one חטאת. It is the case where the person did not know it was an idol, but he knew the acts of worship were forbidden. It is the same choice the תנא made for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise you find
Regarding, in the case of
The different acts of worship

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא גַּבֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
phrases.english: And likewise you find regarding idol worship
for it teaches: not knowing about the idol worship
phrases.notes: He did not realize that what he was worshipping was an idol.

phrases.english: but knowing about the acts of worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא גַּבֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 34 with a matching example
steps.raayaObject: That the תנא chooses the case of not knowing the main prohibition but knowing the acts were forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's teaching about עבודה זרה

steps.title: What does a mistaken act of idol worship look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a concrete case of שגגת עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Unintentional idol worship: what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what a real case of worshipping an idol by mistake would look like. This question sets up a search through several possible cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that one brings a חטאת for idol worship by mistake needs a real case. That is hard to find, because idol worship depends on what the person has in mind. So the גמרא has to find a case that is neither innocent nor fully on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing a sin by mistake, without knowing it was forbidden
Idol worship
What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: Unintentional idol worship, what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 35 mentioned the case of not knowing it was idol worship. Now the גמרא asks what such a case really looks like.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic case in which a person worships an idol by mistake and owes a חטאת.

steps.title: Bowing in an idol house thinking it was a synagogue does not work
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion is a man who bowed in an idol house thinking it was a בית הכנסת. It is rejected because his heart was toward Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose he stood in an idol house, thought it was a synagogue, and bowed. But his heart was toward Heaven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a case: a person bows inside an idol house, thinking it is a בית הכנסת. It rejects this case right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person meant to bow to ה׳, not to the idol. So it is not even a mistaken sin; it is no sin at all. A case of שוגג needs at least some act of worship directed at the idol.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (it is this case)
And he bowed down
His heart is directed toward Heaven

phrases.english: If we say that he stood in a house of idol worship
and thought it was a synagogue, and bowed
But his heart is toward Heaven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to the question in step 36.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the case of bowing in an idol house by mistake.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His intention was toward Heaven, so there is no sin at all, not even a mistaken one.

steps.title: Bowing to a king's statue does not work either
steps.stepSummary: The second suggestion is bowing to a statue. Either he accepted it as a god, which is on purpose and earns סקילה, or he did not, which is nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he saw a statue and bowed to it? If he accepted it as a god, he deserves stoning. If he did not accept it as a god, it is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second case: a person bows to a statue. It shows that this case also fails, no matter how you look at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא splits the case in two. If he truly accepted the statue as a god, he acted on purpose and gets סקילה, not a חטאת. If he did not accept it, he did not worship it at all. Neither side gives us a case of mistaken worship.

keyTerms.meaning: A statue, usually an image of a king
Bowed down (Aramaic)
Accepted it as a god
Death by stoning
It is nothing (no sin at all)

phrases.english: Rather, he saw a statue and bowed to it?
If he accepted it upon himself as a god
he is liable to stoning!
And if he did not accept it as a god
it is nothing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first case fails, the גמרא tries and rejects a second one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects bowing to a statue as the case of mistaken idol worship.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Either it is on purpose (סקילה) or it is not worship at all. There is no middle ground of שוגג.

steps.title: The answer: bowing out of love or fear
steps.stepSummary: The case of mistaken idol worship is bowing to an idol out of love or fear of a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case of bowing out of love or out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the person bowed to an idol because he loved someone or was afraid of someone. He did not realize that this was forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is a real act of bowing to the idol, but without accepting it as a god. The person thought it was allowed as long as he did not truly believe in it. That mistake makes it a case of שוגג.

keyTerms.meaning: Out of love (for a person who asked him to bow)
Out of fear (of a person pressuring him)

phrases.english: Rather, it is out of love or out of fear.
phrases.notes: He bowed to please someone or out of fear of someone, thinking it was allowed since he did not believe in the idol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two cases fail, this gives the working case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mistaken idol worship is bowing out of love or fear, without knowing that this is forbidden.

steps.title: This answer fits אביי but not רבא
steps.stepSummary: The love-or-fear case works for אביי, who holds such a person חייב. For רבא, who holds him פטור, the question returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for אביי, who says he is liable. But for רבא, who says he is exempt, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that its answer only works for one side of a known argument. It asks what case רבא would give. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא argue about someone who bows to an idol out of love or fear. אביי says he is חייב a חטאת, so the answer works for him. רבא says he is פטור, so for רבא this case brings no חטאת, and we are back to having no case of mistaken worship.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (according to one opinion)
Liable (here, to bring a חטאת)
Exempt
What can be said? (introduces a difficulty)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא are not arguing about what mistaken idol worship is in general. They argue about this one case, bowing out of love or fear. Only אביי makes him bring a חטאת, so only for אביי can it serve as the example.

phrases.english: This works well according to Abaye, who says he is liable,
but according to Rava, who says he is exempt,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְאַבַּיֵּי דְּאָמַר חַיָּיב אֶלָּא לְרָבָא דְּאָמַר פָּטוּר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 39 by showing it depends on one side of an argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that mistaken idol worship means bowing out of love or fear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא holds that bowing out of love or fear is פטור, so for him this cannot be the case that brings a חטאת. We still need a case that works for רבא.
